app.title: population-pulse
app.summary: The person picks a date range, then checks whether the latest week of the outcome series is high, normal or low for the time of year, and how fresh each source is. They look at all the weekly series together as z-scores on one timeline, with event markers. Then they choose one candidate driver and scan lags 0 to 8 weeks for cross-correlation, corrected for multiple comparisons. At the chosen lag they fit a surge logistic regression and a count regression, and check those fits out of sample with walk-forward validation. Finally they check whether the drivers are confounded with each other, correct every driver-lag test together, and can download the aligned weekly table as CSV.

task.text: Find out which candidate weekly signals lead an outcome series, at which lag and how robustly, before running confirmatory studies.

data.text: Several sources of time series, each brought to one weekly timeline, plus a dated list of events. One series is the outcome and the others are candidate drivers.
data.item: one week's aggregated value for one signal

stage.text: exploring and analysing candidate leading indicators of an outcome series, before confirmatory event studies

mechanism.text: A sidebar date range filters every view. Three tabs follow: an overview of status and data freshness, a z-scored multi-series timeline with event rules, and an analysis tab. In the analysis tab, choosing a driver drives a lag-correlation bar chart, regressions at a lag set with a slider, walk-forward validation, a driver-by-driver correlation heatmap with VIF, and a correction table covering every driver and lag.

field.text: lagged cross-correlation and count regression of weekly syndromic surveillance data in epidemiology

workflow.name: test which candidate series lead an outcome series, and at what lag

steps.here: Pre-ingested weekly signals load automatically: local Parquet first, then a remote data branch, then synthetic samples. The person picks a city.

steps.step: filter to the period that matters
steps.here: 1Y / 2Y / 5Y / All preset buttons, or From and To dates, restrict every signal before it is aligned to weeks.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Metrics show the latest outcome week against its seasonal baseline, with an elevated, normal or below banner, a table of events and a per-signal freshness table. A multi-select chooses which series to overlay as z-scores, with dashed event rules and a provisional-data line.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The person picks a driver and can choose to deseasonalize first. Bars show the correlation at each lag from 0 to 8 weeks, with 95% Fisher CIs. The best lag is reported with raw and Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected p-values, and warnings appear when it fails correction or overlaps the runner-up lag.

steps.step: fit a model at the chosen lag and check it out of sample
steps.here: Sliders set the driver lag and the surge quantile, and a select picks a Poisson or Negative-Binomial family. The tab fits a surge logistic regression (AUC, pseudo-R²) and a count GLM (coefficient, p, AIC), then compares in-sample and walk-forward out-of-sample AUC and MAE.

steps.step: check the drivers against each other and correct across every test
steps.here: A heatmap of deseasonalized correlations between drivers, with a VIF table, shows confounding. A table applies Benjamini-Hochberg correction to every driver-lag test together.
An expander shows the aligned weekly table, with a Download as CSV button.

distinctive: Each series is judged against its own seasonal baseline (a rolling seasonal residual), so 'elevated' means high for the time of year, and correlations are deseasonalized by default to avoid spurious winter co-trends.
The most recent outcome weeks are provisional and get revised upward, so they are marked on the timeline and masked out of every correlation and regression automatically.

Multiple-comparisons correction happens at two levels: across one driver's lag sweep, and across the full driver-by-lag family. Lag picks whose confidence intervals overlap the runner-up are flagged as ambiguous.
Overdispersed weekly counts are fitted with Negative-Binomial as the default rather than Poisson, and in-sample fits are set against expanding-window walk-forward scores to expose overfitting.
Signals with different units are z-scored only for display; the analysis uses the raw values, and sub-series on different scales (one per pathogen) are split out before weekly summing.
